subtitle: Steakhouse night at the station
description: Steakhouse night at the station. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Grilled NY Strip with Herb Butter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season and temper
steps.instruction: Pat steaks dry. Salt heavily 40 minutes ahead (or right before if rushed). Pepper just before cooking. Let meat sit out 20 minutes — cold centers overcook the exterior.

steps.title: Grill over high heat
steps.instruction: Grill over high heat (450–500°F surface) 3–5 minutes per side for strip to 130°F medium-rare. Flank: sear 4 minutes per side, then medium until 125°F; rest and slice thin against the grain.

steps.title: Baste with herb butter
steps.instruction: Melt butter with garlic and parsley. Rest steaks 8 minutes tented with foil, then slice and spoon butter over. Hold on warm trays at 180°F no more than 20 minutes.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Grilled NY Strip with Herb Butter onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve on sheet trays
steps.instruction: Grilled NY Strip with Herb Butter goes out sliced on trays with extra herb butter melting on top — crew grabs with tongs, not forks and knives.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Grilled NY Strip with Herb Butter — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.

tonightSpread: Plate Grilled NY Strip with Herb Butter with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Grilled NY Strip with Herb Butter on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.

Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.

leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
